subject: AB_Snow_Polluted
maker: ALPHA_BIOMES_RETIRE_THE_LAST_PLANT_DONOR run (installed 9967aa8641, judged by eye itself)
judge: fresh Opus sessions launched by this item's run (/mnt/d/ClaudeWork/scratch/judge32/run.py on art_calibration's schema and contract check); none made the art

verdicts.why: The brief does not decide tile seams. terrain.png has a darker 1-px frame on all four edges. Mean RGB is about (132,127,122) on col 0, (129,124,119) on col 1023 and (132,128,122) on row 0, against about (142,137,132) inside, so the frame is 10 to 13 levels darker. The texture content itself carries on across the wrap. But tiled_2x2.png shows a thin dark grid line at every join, 2 px wide where two frames meet, and you can see it at full view. The game repeats this file across every polluted cell, so the line would form a grid over the map. No lettered constraint (A1 to F1) covers seamless tiling, so I cannot REDO on it (see proposals), and I will not KEEP a picture with a visible seam grid.
verdicts.notes: Everything else passes. E1: this is our own drawing, not the donor. Its luminance correlates with donor_standin.png at only r=0.015, and the motifs differ: blotchy grey-brown snow against the donor's flat grey ripple relief. No canon entry, no facings, no owner keep, no notes from him (subject.json). Palette: mid-grey, mean L about 139, with olive-brown dirty patches. It reads as soiled snow next to the bright blue-white sibling_unpolluted.png, which is not a keep, so B3 does not bind. Patch edges look a little like procedural cell-noise. Inspected at 3x, the fine detail is a painterly grain, not a flat script fill, so E2 is not refused.
verdicts.seen: A darker 1-px border round the whole file. In tiled_2x2.png it shows as a straight grey cross at x=1023/1024 and y=1023/1024, cutting the snow pattern.

proposals: Add a terrain constraint: a terrain texture must tile without a visible seam. Its edge rows and columns must match the interior in mean value within about 3 levels, and no line may show at the joins of the 2x2 tile. Evidence: terrain.png edge columns and rows are 10 to 13 levels darker than the interior (col 1023 mean about 129 against about 142), and tiled_2x2.png shows a dark grid line at every join. A one-pass fix is easy: drop the 1-px border and rebuild it from the wrapped interior, or regenerate with wrap padding.

Add a line saying a polluted terrain variant should keep the base material's texture character, so it reads as the same ground made dirty. Evidence: terrain.png has blotchy cell-noise clumps where sibling_unpolluted.png has a crystalline powder grain. They still read as related snow, so this is advisory only.
looks.look: first: full inspection of the installed pictures

verdicts.notes: Repair check, second and last look. I looked only at what the repair changed: the 1-px frame and the 96-px blend band. (1) The frame is gone. Mean luminance is 136.5 on col 0, 135.9 on col 1, 136.9 on col 1023 and 136.8 at col 512. Row 0 is 140.0, row 1 is 139.8 and row 1023 is 140.1. Before the repair the edges were 10 to 13 levels darker. (2) The wrap is continuous. The mean |L| step across the wrap is 3.5 horizontal and 3.2 vertical, against a 2.7 mean step between neighbouring interior pixels (about 1.2 to 1.3x). At full view, tiled_2x2.png shows no grid line at x=1024 or y=1024. A 512-px crop centred on the four-way join and a 3x crop across the vertical join show no line, no step in tone and no cut motif: the blotches run across the join. (3) The repair touched only the band: the mean difference from before_repair.png is 3.0 over the whole file, 0.62 inside a 48-px margin and 0.00 inside a 96-px margin. So the interior that the first judge passed is unchanged byte for byte. (4) Ghosting: the band is slightly softer. Its high-frequency step is 2.43 against 2.70 in the middle, and its luminance std is 11.5 against 14.1. At 3x a few blotch edges in the band look faintly doubled. By eye, at full view and in the tiled view, this does not show as a stripe or a repeated ghost motif, and I could not find the band without measuring. No lettered line covers it. The first judge's other findings still hold on the unchanged interior. E1: this is our own drawing, not donor_standin.png (that is a flat grey ripple relief). E2: a painterly grain, not a script fill. B3: no keep on sibling_unpolluted.png (subject.json), and the candidate reads as soiled snow beside it. No owner keep, no notes from him, no canon entry (subject.json).
verdicts.seen: Repaired file: no dark frame on any edge. The 2x2 tiling joins without a visible line or tone step. A slightly softer, lower-contrast 96-px border band, visible only by measurement or at 3x, with faint doubling of a few blotch edges.
verdicts.why: The repair removed the seam that made the first judge answer UNSURE. Seamless tiling is still not a lettered constraint, so it is not the basis of this KEEP. It is recorded in proposals.

proposals: Add a lettered terrain constraint, e.g. 'D5. A terrain file tiles seamlessly: no edge frame, and the wrap step is within about 1.5x the interior pixel step, judged on a 2x2 tiling.' Evidence: before_repair.png had a 1-px frame 10 to 13 levels darker, which formed a grid line at every repeat in tiled_2x2.png. No line from A1 to F1 could refuse it, so the first look could only answer UNSURE.

Note for the terrain repair recipe, not a constraint: a half-shift blend band softens texture a little. Here the 96-px band measures std 11.5 against 14.1 in the interior and high-frequency step 2.43 against 2.70. It is not visible at full view in tiled_2x2.png, but a wider band or a lower-contrast source could show as a soft stripe at each join. A future seamless-tiling line could add 'the border band keeps interior contrast within about 20%'.

window_verdict.basis: Both looks found no lettered line (A1-F1) broken; no REDO and no refusal record. The first look's UNSUREs named one point no line covers: a 1-px dark frame and a weak wrap step, a grid line at every repeat in game (measured: frame 3-26 levels, wrap up to 6x; donors 0-2 and 1.0-1.2x). The second look checked repair v1 and found it drew the old wrap seam at the midline of each border band (UNSURE on 3; measured on all 15). Repair v3 removes the frame and cross-fades the wrap without a shifted copy: measured frame <= 0.8, wrap 0.97-1.23x, worst straight line in the file and across the wrap <= 1.52x the median step (donors 1.5-8.7x), and a 2x2 tile shows no line by eye. The brief allows no third look (§When the look is enough, and when to stop), so v3 stands on its measurements. A Slime UNSURE on the second look was for the missing play-zoom input, which the brief does not define for a terrain (proposal).
